transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-05
Time: 10:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Maya Singh (AstraHealth CTO), Liam O'Connor (Head of MLOps), Sofia Reyes (SRE), Devon Park (Data Eng)

Summary:
Quick sync to review last week's benchmark results vs their baseline provider, discuss tuning options (batching, quantization, KV cache), and confirm next steps for an on-prem smoke test and SOC2 materials. We covered methodology discrepancies and agreed to rerun p99 traces with warmed KV cache.

Topics:
- Benchmark numbers (p95,p99 latencies, throughput QPS)
- Methodology: seq lengths, concurrency, tokenization differences
- Tuning knobs: batching, continuous batching window, kv cache hits, quantization profile
- Security/compliance & on-prem smoke test logistics
- Next steps and owners

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everybody, thanks for joining. quick agenda, we'll go through the benchmark sheet i shared, highlight gaps vs baseline, then priya will go into tuning suggestions and we'll close with next steps.
[00:18] Maya Singh: thanks, alex. we skimmed the sheet, quick call out, baseline provider numbers are what our infra team runs in prod right now so want to understand apples-to-apples.
[00:30] Priya Kapoor: totally, that's the goal. note up front there were two methodology diffs — tokenization chunking and sequence lengths. your baseline tests were at 1k token max whereas we used a 512 median plus tail 1k in a few runs. that changed p99 by ~10-15% in some cases.
[00:55] Liam O'Connor: yeah we did 1k to be conservative but our live distribution is 300-600 tokens 75% of the time.
[01:08] Alex Chen: ok good — priya, can you summarize the headline numbers vs baseline from the sheet?
[01:15] Priya Kapoor: sure. baseline provider p95 for our 512-ish workload was ~180ms, p99 ~420ms, throughput about 120 qps at 12 concurrent workers. our Redwood hosted run on the same model variant showed p95 ~125ms, p99 ~310ms, throughput ~200 qps at 12 concurrency. cost per token was lower on Redwood when using continuous batching + prefix caching — about 18% savings on compute cost in these runs. note: these are initial numbers, some runs didn't have kv cache pre-warmed so p99 fluctuates.
[01:45] Sofia Reyes: that p99 difference is significant — can you confirm test harness parity? are we using same batch sizes, same software tokenizers?
[01:53] Priya Kapoor: good q. we used your harness but swapped in our runtime client so there are small client side differences; but we ran a cross-check where we used your harness + our worker and numbers were within ~5%. the larger diffs came from cache warm state and quantization profile — baseline is running int8 static quant while our run used grp-q4_0 mix (we used a model quant profile optimized for latency).
[02:24] Devon Park: when you say q4_0 mix, is that lossy? we can't afford hallucination regressions.
[02:30] Priya Kapoor: it's a tradeoff, q4_0 is nearly lossless for our tests but we can run a quality eval set you provided; we already ran a quick rouge/emt/llm eval — no significant deltas on our sample, but we'll run your full eval.
[02:45] Maya Singh: can we get the raw logs / traces for p99? our SLA team wants to see request/response traces and kernel metrics.
[02:52] Alex Chen: yes — we'll share the traces. priya will attach flame traces and p95/p99 histograms.
[03:00] Priya Kapoor: moving to tuning recommendations: 1) warm the KV cache before p99 runs (we saw p99 drop by ~80ms when KV warm), 2) increase continuous batching window slightly for throughput tests (helps for small seqs), 3) pin model variant for fairness (same quant and tokenizer) and 4) use same concurrency profile as prod (you said 12 workers).
[03:23] Liam O'Connor: for throughput, baseline claims 150 qps steady, you ran 200 qps — what's the hardware parity?
[03:30] Priya Kapoor: hardware was same family (A100 equivalent) for both — we matched GPU SKU and driver stack. where Redwood benefited is runtime optimizations: attention kernel selection and better kv cache eviction heuristics. that plus continuous batching gives higher effective QPS.
[03:50] Sofia Reyes: any differences in network latency? their baseline is colocated in our same region, we set tests in us-west and disabled cross-region routing for parity.
[03:58] Priya Kapoor: yep we matched region and network. small jitter noted in one baseline run — could be noisy neighbor, we flagged it in the sheet.
[04:10] Maya Singh: curious about private deployment numbers — if we run Redwood private (VPC) will numbers hold?
[04:17] Priya Kapoor: good question. in our internal tests private deployment numbers are similar; we have additional overhead for control-plane comms but we can run an on-prem smoke test. typically the delta is <5% if the infra is equivalent and KV cache is local.
[04:33] Alex Chen: ok — so main ask for us is to rerun p99 with KV warm and same tokenization, plus a cost model overlay.
[04:41] Priya Kapoor: yes. also we'll include p99 traces and flame graphs.
[04:47] Devon Park: any considerations for autoscaling? baseline uses quick scale up which causes cold starts on some pods.
[04:53] Priya Kapoor: our autoscaler supports pre-warm and graceful scale-up policies; we can simulate scale events and include that in the smoke test.
[05:03] Maya Singh: security/compliance — we need SOC2 posture and KMS integration notes for the RFP.
[05:10] Alex Chen: i'll send our SOC2 summary and KMS docs, plus the private deployment checklist.
[05:14] Liam O'Connor: on the cost model, can you break down per-token compute + infra + egress?
[05:19] Priya Kapoor: yes we'll break out compute (GPU hours/token), disk/network egress, and show reserved vs burst cost for Dedicated.
[05:25] Sofia Reyes: quick nit — can you include a column for seq length distribution? that will help us map to our prod cost.
[05:31] Alex Chen: will do.
[05:33] Priya Kapoor: one more note — when you run your baseline provider, ask for p99 with kv cold and warmed states; some vendors report only warmed numbers which skews the comparison.
[05:43] Maya Singh: noted.
[05:46] Alex Chen: let's recap next steps — alex share sheet, priya run the warm p99 traces, maya provide seq distributions and security contacts, schedule on-prem smoke test for week of 3/16.
[05:58] Devon Park: fine with that timeline.
[06:00] Alex Chen: ok thanks all, we'll follow up in email.

(End of recording)

Recap / Notes (auto):
- Redwood currently showing better median/p95 and higher throughput in initial tests given continuous batching and KV cache benefits.
- Main variance driver: seq-length distribution, KV cache warm state, and quantization profile.
- Agreed reruns with warmed KV cache and matched tokenizer/seq length.
- Redwood to provide traces, cost model, and SOC2/KMS docs.
